analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date on line 3 and adds a paragraph after the inference_response_chunk table, around head lines 757-765. The paragraph documents streamed auto tool calls: choices[].delta.tool_calls entries share an index, the first carries id/type/name and empty arguments, and later ones carry argument fragments that consumers concatenate. This describes chunking of the already-encrypted response payload and the source symbol streamChatCompletionFrames.

The change adds no code, wire field, or trust grant. The encryption contract is unchanged: the base text at line 754 still says `data` is empty when E2E encryption is active and `encrypted_data` carries the payload. Fragmenting tool-call arguments across chunks is inside the encrypted payload, so plaintext exposure (T-008, A-001) is not changed by this text.

The documentation is not accurate against the implementation, because the source is not supplied. I could not verify that streamChatCompletionFrames behaves as described, that each fragment is encrypted per chunk, or that fail-closed behavior on encryption failure holds for the new streamed tool-call path. Those are open questions for any code review of the runtime change. Nothing in the supplied evidence shows a regression, so there are no findings.

The other examined units, 4-6 (base text for protocol messages), are unchanged context. They include the prefix-cache v2 receipts (T-041), the retirement protocol, and the App Attest hardware binding, and none of them is modified by this diff.
